key_insight: In epitaxial CsPbBr3 single crystals, terahertz and Hall mobilities match closely, indicating intrinsic, defect-limited charge transport across macroscopic length scales.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical benchmark and measurement strategy for identifying truly high-quality perovskite materials for optoelectronic devices.
method: Concurrent Hall-effect and optical pump-terahertz probe (OPTP) measurements on the same single-crystal sample
Compare local ultrafast mobility with macroscopic steady-state transport mobility across temperatures
Use epitaxial CsPbBr3 single crystals to test whether transport remains intrinsic beyond microscopic length scales
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent room-temperature mobilities of about 30 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1 from both Hall and OPTP methods, with similar band-like temperature dependence and power-law exponents.
watch_item: Results are shown for a dedicated epitaxial single-crystal platform, so translation to polycrystalline films or defect-rich devices may not preserve the same mobility agreement.
paper_title: Matching Terahertz and Hall Mobilities as a Hallmark of Intrinsic Charge Transport in Metal-Halide Perovskites
